flawed_step: Section 4 (Proof of Theorem PreobZZ), lines 0551-0559: the asserted bound |M_chi(x,y_0)| << x e^{-c(log x)^{3/5}(log_2 x)^{-1/5}} for y_0 asymp q asymp exp(c(log X)^{2/5}(log_2 X)^{1/5}) and X^c << x << X, justified only by 'By an argument similar to that of Koukoulopoulos'. It is never proved, and it is not an independent input: combined with the paper's own (correct) lower bound at line 0547 it is quantitatively equivalent to the very conclusion beta_0 <= 1 - c/log q. The proof of Theorem PreobZZ is therefore circular.
counterexample:
Explicit parameter trace showing the asserted bound already excludes exactly the zeros Theorem PreobZZ claims to exclude, hence cannot be an input to its proof. Take the constant in lines 0553-0554 to be 1, so q = ceil(exp((log X)^{2/5}(log_2 X)^{1/5})) and y_0 = q, and set X = e^{10^{10}}. Then log X = 1.0e10, log_2 X = 23.0259, (log X)^{2/5} = 1.0e4, (log_2 X)^{1/5} = 1.8726, so log q = log y_0 = 1.87259e4, and L := (log X)^{3/5}(log_2 X)^{-1/5} = 5.34019e5. Let chi be a real primitive even character mod q with chi(2)=1 and suppose it has a real zero at beta_0 = 1 - 10^{-3}/log q = 1 - 5.34019e-8, i.e. exactly the kind of zero Theorem PreobZZ asserts cannot exist (1-beta_0 = 10^{-3}/log q). Then (1-beta_0) log X = 534.02, so X^{1+beta_0} = X^2 e^{-534.02}, and the paper's own displayed lower bound (line 0547) gives
  int_1^X |M_chi(x,y_0)| dx >> X^{1+beta_0}/(q^{3/2} log y_0) = X^2 exp(-534.02 - 1.5*1.87259e4 - ln(1.87259e4)) = X^2 e^{-28632.7}.
Now feed in the asserted bound of line 0558 with an explicit constant c_1: since the integrand is dominated by x near X, and x < X^c contributes only O(X^{2c}),
  int_1^X |M_chi(x,y_0)| dx << X^2 e^{-c_1 L (1+o(1))} = X^2 e^{-c_1 * 5.34019e5 (1+o(1))}.
The two are contradictory as soon as c_1 * 5.34019e5 > 28632.7, i.e. for every c_1 > 0.0537. So for any admissible constant c_1 >= 0.06 the asserted bound at line 0558 is FALSE for this chi -- the assertion by itself forbids beta_0 = 1 - 10^{-3}/log q. In other words, line 0558 is not a lemma the argument may import; it is (up to the value of the constant) a restatement of the conclusion at line 0562, and the intervening lines 0547-0562 are a rescaling of one into the other. Concretely: with X = e^{10^{10}}, q = e^{18725.9}, y_0 = q, the number pair (c_1, 1-beta_0) = (0.06, 5.34019e-8) satisfies every hypothesis stated in lines 0553-0555 yet is excluded by line 0558 and by line 0562 simultaneously, so no derivation of 0562 from 0558 can add information. Consistently with this, the reference actually cited (Koukoulopoulos, pretentious multiplicative functions) proves mean-value bounds that carry an explicit exceptional-character term for precisely this reason, so it does not supply the asserted uniform bound; and the paper itself flags the exactly analogous bound for the principal case as conditional at lines 0262-0267 ('if l_0 WERE the level ... then we WOULD have').
reasoning_summary: Verified in order. (1) Theorem 1 (inversion formula, lines 0165-0183): the stated beta is exactly the Dirichlet inverse of alpha -- with alpha = alpha(1)(delta + h), h(1)=0, one gets alpha^{-1} = (1/alpha(1)) sum_k (-1)^k h^{*k}, matching the displayed k-fold sums with denominators (-alpha(1))^k; the side condition n_i not in {1,n} is equivalent to n_i > 1 for k >= 2 and the k=1 term is written out separately, so the formula is right. The conclusion then follows since sum_{n<=X} beta(n) F(X/n) = sum_{k<=X}(beta*alpha)(k) G(X/k) = G(X). Correct (modulo the unstated hypothesis alpha(1) != 0). (2) Application (lines 0200-0219): the Euler-product identity is trivially true; the Dirichlet series of the indicator alpha(n,y) is zeta(s) prod_{p<=y}(1-p^{-s}) and that of the coefficient function of M(x,y) is (1-2^{-s})/(zeta(s) prod_{p<=y}(1-p^{-s})^{-1})^{-1} = zeta(s)^{-1} prod_{3<=p<=y}(1-p^{-s})^{-1} (using mu(2m) = -mu(m) for m odd), so U(X) = sum_n alpha(n,y) M(X/n,y) is correct; U(X/n)=1 iff X/2 < n <= X gives (PreobMXyId); beta(n,y) = sum_k (-1)^k d_k^*(n,y) is correct since alpha(n_1)...alpha(n_k)=1 iff P^-(n)>y. Spot-checked numerically: (y=2,X=3) gives M(3,2) = beta(2,2)+beta(3,2) = 0-1 = -1, correct; (y=3,X=9) gives M(9,3) = sum_{n=5}^{9} beta(n,3) = -2, matching mu(1)+mu(2)+mu(5)+mu(7) = -2. Only defect: beta(1,y) = 1 but the displayed formula gives an empty sum 0 at n=1 -- immaterial (affects only X<2). (3) Truncation at k <= log X/log y (line 0222): correct, since each factor > y forces y^k < n <= X. (4) Recursion d_k^* = d_k' - sum_j binom(k,j) d_j^* (line 0227): correct for n>1 by counting how many of the k factors equal 1 (binomial coefficients agree by symmetry); off by a constant at n=1, which only shifts the constant term of F_{l,y}(s). Hence F_{l,y} is a linear combination of zeta^k prod (1-p^{-s})^k, as claimed. (5) Section 2 numerical example, X=6: verified Lemma 1 ((log - d)*mu = Lambda - 1), all six matrix rows, and every entry of the solution vector, e.g. b_4 = -(alpha(4)+alpha(2)^2) = -(log 2)^2 + 2log 2 - 1 and b_6 = -(alpha(6) + 2 alpha(2)alpha(3)) = -2 log2 log3 + 3log2 + 3log3 - 4 -- both match the paper exactly. (6) Section 3 proof: the Cramer's-rule setup and the cofactor expression for beta(n) are correct; the row operation r_i <- S_i r_i + r_{i-1} is written sloppily (it multiplies the determinant by prod S_i, never mentioned, and degenerates when some S_i = 0), but I checked it explicitly for n=4 and for n=6 (X=6) and in both cases the final diagonal entry is exactly alpha(1)beta(n), so the sketch is recoverable rather than wrong. (7) Section 4: the Mellin formula (line 0487) is correct and is where chi(2)=1 is needed; g_chi is entire; the contour shift to sigma = 1+beta_0-1/log y_0, the residue at s = 1+beta_0, and the lower bound U >> X^{1+beta_0}/log y_0 all check out (the truncated Euler product is >= prod_{p<=y_0}(1+p^{-beta_0})^{-1} >> 1/log y_0, and X^{-1/log y_0} log y_0 = o(1/log y_0) for the stated y_0); the tail estimate along sigma = lambda reproduces e^{lambda+4}/(lambda-2) << X exactly as claimed; the convexity bound L(-1+it,chi) << q^{3/2}|t|^{3/2} and |r_lambda(H)| << q^{3/2} are fine (the written integral diverges at t=0 only because the |t|^{3/2} numerator is used outside its range; near t=0 the integrand is O(q^{3/2}) and the bound survives). So the chain down to X^{1+beta_0}/(q^{3/2} log y_0) << int_1^X |M_chi| is sound. FAILURE at lines 0551-0559: the bound on |M_chi(x,y_0)| that closes the argument is asserted with no proof, and the explicit trace in the counterexample field shows it is quantitatively equivalent to the conclusion beta_0 <= 1 - c/log q, so the proof of Theorem PreobZZ (an unconditional Landau-Siegel bound) is circular. Secondary, non-fatal: the Definition's assertion at lines 0253-0256 needs the hypothesised bounds at x/2 as well as at x with the same l_0, which is not what is postulated.
